events.title: Jan Hus Burned at the Stake
events.description: The Bohemian religious reformer Jan Hus was executed for heresy at the Council of Constance. He was burned at the stake after refusing to recant his teachings.
events.significance: Hus became a martyr and a national symbol in Bohemia. His followers' anger helped set off the Hussite Wars, and his ideas influenced the later Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Thomas More Is Executed
events.description: Sir Thomas More, the former Lord Chancellor of England, was beheaded for treason. He had refused to accept King Henry VIII as supreme head of the Church of England.
events.significance: More's death became a lasting symbol of conscience against state power. The Catholic Church later canonized him as a saint.

events.title: Pasteur Gives First Rabies Vaccination
events.description: Louis Pasteur gave the first successful rabies inoculation to nine-year-old Joseph Meister, who had been bitten by a rabid dog.
events.significance: The treatment showed that vaccines could be used after exposure to a disease. It was a landmark for medicine and public health.

events.title: Althea Gibson Wins Wimbledon
events.description: Althea Gibson became the first African American to win a Wimbledon singles title when she took the women's championship at the All England Club.
events.significance: Gibson broke a major color barrier in international tennis. She opened the way for later Black champions in the sport.
